before: font-weight changes visual thickness, font-style can request italic text, and text-align positions inline content within its line box. These style choices do not turn a paragraph into a semantic heading or emphasis element.

700 commonly requests bold weight; the available font decides how that weight is drawn. italic may use an italic face or a synthesized slant. text-align:start follows writing direction rather than always meaning left. Use HTML headings and emphasis when the content’s meaning requires them, not just because a CSS rule looks similar.

after: Typography means the way letters are styled and arranged. `font-weight` changes how thick letters look. `font-style: italic` requests slanted letters. These settings do not change a paragraph into a heading.
`text-align` positions text within its line. The value `start` follows the writing direction: left for left-to-right text, and right for right-to-left text.
Keep both pieces as paragraphs for this project. When real content needs a heading or emphasis, use the matching HTML element. Making words bold or italic only changes their appearance.
